title: Fabrication of Inverted Colloidal Crystal Poly(ethylene glycol) Scaffold: A Three-dimensional Cell Culture Platform for Liver Tissue Engineering
protocol: Prepare polystyrene lattices with diameter of 6 mm and 8-13 layers of beads.
Cut tips off from 0.2 ml boil-proof microcentrifuge tubes at the 40 µl level to create molds.
Adhere the top of the cut-tubes to microscope cover glass slips using water-proof glue.
Pipette out water suspension containing PS spheres and add 18 ml of 70% ethanol solution into a vial.
Place sphere solution in an ultrasonic bath to loosen aggregated spheres.
Wash PS spheres several times with ethanol to remove water and water-soluble components completely.
Pipette 100 µl of ethanol into the molds.
Cut the top of a 200 µl micropipette tip by 4 mm.
Pipette 25 µl of the spheres into the mold twice using the 200 µl micropipette to achieve a total volume of 50 µl in each mold.
Place molds on a rocking shaker at 120 rpm overnight.
Check arrangement of spheres in each mold under an optical microscope and correct if necessary by adding 50 µl of 70% ethanol and shaking manually.
Let the ethanol evaporate at room temperature for two nights.
Anneal PS beads by placing mold and bead complex in a 130 °C furnace for 6 hr.
Synthesize PEGDA macromers using established protocols.
Prepare a 50% (w/v) PEGDA solution in de-ionized water.
Centrifuge the PEGDA solution at 4,713 x g until completely dissolved.
For ECM conjugated ICC scaffolds, dissolve an additional 10% (w/v) Acryloyl-PEG-NHS in the 50% PEGDA solution.
Prepare a 20% (w/v) stock solution of 2-hydroxy-4'-(2-hydroxyethoxy)-2-methylpropiophenone (PI) in 70% ethanol.
Add 50 µl of PI stock solution per 1 ml of 50% PEGDA.
Vortex the mixture for 1 min to reach a homogenous solution.
Remove molds from glass slide and remove glue from molds.
Push lattices out carefully using a spatula and place each into a 1.5 ml tube.
Pipette 300 µl of PEGDA solution and centrifuge at 845 x g for 5 min.
Remove the lattice from the tube using tweezers.
Blot dry excess PEGDA solution on gloves.
Place the lattice on a paraffin film-covered glass with the flat circular surface facing up.
Expose the PEGDA solution infiltrated scaffold to 365 nm ultraviolet light (10.84 mW/cm2) for 5 min using a UV spot lamp.
Place PEGDA-polymerized crystal lattices in new vials (around 10 lattices per vial).
Add 20 ml of tetrahydrofuran (THF) to the vials containing the lattices.
Shake the vials on an orbital shaker at 300 rpm.
Change THF at least 3 times with an interval of 1-2 hr.
Check if PS spheres are dissolved by putting water into the used THF solution and observing the solution color.
Repeat step if the PS spheres are not properly dissolved.
Prepare a 50 ml centrifuge tube with 2 ml of 70% ethanol per scaffold.
Place the scaffolds in the tube using a spatula.
Allow the scaffolds to soak in ethanol for 1 hr.
Carefully pour the ethanol out and replace with phosphate buffer saline (PBS) (2 ml per scaffold).
Centrifuge at 524 x g for 3 min to remove bubbles.
Change PBS a few times with an interval of 1-2 hr.
Prepare a 50 ml centrifuge tube containing Collagen type I stock solution (1 ml per scaffold).
Transfer sterilized scaffolds to the tube using a spatula.
Centrifuge the tube at 524 x g for 3 min.
Shake the scaffolds at 400 rpm on an orbital shaker for 30 min.
Keep the tube in the refrigerator overnight.
Wash the scaffolds with PBS twice before use by submerging them in fresh PBS and then aspirating the PBS.
Fix scaffolds with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Serially dehydrate the fixed scaffolds in 25%, 50%, 75%, 95%, and 100% ethanol solutions.
Store the scaffolds at -80°C until the ethanol evaporates completely.
Dry the samples in a freeze drier for 48 hours.
Affix the sample onto a sample holder using carbon tape.
Place the affixed sample into a sputter coater.
After automatic vacuuming, coat the sample with a Pt film of 10 nm thickness by sputtering for 60 seconds at 20 mA.
Image ICC scaffolds using SEM at a voltage of 5 kV.
Analyze SEM micrographs using image analysis software to measure pore and interconnection diameters.
Fluorescently tag the collagen on the scaffold using antibodies (1:100) against type I collagen.
Visualize the conjugated collagen without cells using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM).
Culture Huh-7.5 cells at a density of 2-2.5 x 10^6 cells/ml in 100 mm cell culture dishes with 10 ml DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 100 U/ml penicillin-streptomycin.
Change the media every three days until cells reach 75-80% confluency.
Prepare scaffolds for cell seeding in a BSC.
Carefully place the scaffolds in a 24-well plate with the flat surface facing up.
Wash the scaffold by pipetting 2 ml PBS to each well containing a scaffold.
Aspirate the PBS and pipette 2 ml fresh PBS into each well.
Aspirate the PBS and pipette 2 ml of growth media into each well; leave for 30 min.
Aspirate the media and allow the scaffold to dry for 1 hr.
Detach confluent Huh-7.5 cells from the culture plate using trypsin digestion method.
Aspirate media from plate, add 4 ml PBS to wash adherent cells and then aspirate PBS.
Pipette 0.75-1 ml 0.25% trypsin into plate and place in an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 3 min.
Remove plate from incubator and pipette 5 ml media to stop the trypsin reaction.
Pipette media, detached cells, and trypsin mixture into a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 524 x g for 3 min, remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5 ml media.
Count cells using a hemocytometer to calculate the volume of cell suspension that contains cells at target number.
Slowly pipette 25 µl of cell suspension directly on top of each scaffold.
Place the 24-well plate in the incubator.
After 12 hr, transfer the scaffolds carefully with the use of a spatula into a new 24-well plate.
Pipette 2 ml of media into each well containing transferred scaffolds.
Place the 24-well plate in the incubator.
Change the media every 3 days or depending on when media is collected for protein secretion analysis.
Aspirate media in each well containing a scaffold using a pipette.
Pipette 500 μl of a solution containing 4 µM calcein AM and 8 µM ethidium homo-dimer-1 into each well.
Incubate samples at 37°C for 1 hour.
Cover the plates with foil to protect from light during removal from the incubator.
Image stained cells using CLSM.
Create a standard curve for the ICC platform by plotting absorbance (OD) versus given cell number.
Determine cell seeding numbers, N0, for the standard curve.
Choose a range including estimated cell numbers in the experiment.
Seed cells into ICC scaffolds with one N0 per scaffold using 25 μl volume.
Transfer scaffolds to another 24-well plate well after 6 hours.
Incubate the 24-well plate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Pipette 500 μl of 1x MSR solution into each well containing a scaffold.
From each well, transfer 100 μl into a 96-well plate well.
As a blank, pipette 100 μl of fresh 1x MSR solution into different wells on the 96-well plate.
Manually remove any bubbles using a dry pipette tip.
Cover the 96-well plate with foil to protect from light.
Measure OD at λ = 450 nm reading using a spectrophotometer.
Subtract the blank OD from other values to find accurate OD51.
Count the number of cells (NL) remaining in the well after transferring the scaffold.
Use 300 μl of trypsin to trypsinize the cells.
Calculate the actual cell number using the formula NA = N0 - NL.
Make a standard curve by plotting OD vs. actual cell number (NA).
Estimate the cell number in experiments based on the standard curve.
Dilute the collected media from step 3.7 depending on the number of cells seeded and amount collected for ELISA.
Analyze protein secretion by Huh-7.5 cells using ELISA.
Immunostain specific intracellular proteins, enzymes, and structural components as well as nuclei for qualitative cell function analysis.
Aspirate media (from step 3.7) from the cell-laden ICC scaffolds.
Pipette 2 ml PBS to wash the cell-laden ICC scaffolds.
Pipette 1 ml of 4% PFA and incubate at room temperature for 5 min for fixation.
Wash the scaffolds 3 times with 2 ml PBS.
Incubate scaffolds in 1 ml of 0.1% surfactant (4-(1,1,3,3-tetramethylbutyl)phenyl-polyethylene glycol) for 30 min to permeabilize membranes.
Wash the scaffolds 3 times with 2 ml PBS.
Pipette 500 µl of 1% BSA and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour to block non-specific binding.
Pipette 500 µl of 1% BSA solution into a 15 ml tube.
Add 4.5 ml of 0.1% surfactant solution to the 15 ml tube to produce a total of 5 ml of 0.1% BSA solution.
Pipette 98 µl of the 0.1% BSA solution into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2 µl of primary antibody to the microcentrifuge tube to create a 1:50 (primary antibody: 0.1% BSA) solution.
Pipette 40 µl of the primary antibody solution onto the scaffold.
Cover the scaffold with paraffin film.
Wrap the 24 well plate with aluminum foil and store at 4 °C overnight.
Wash 3x with 2 ml PBS, shaking gently between washes.
Prepare a diluted biotinylated secondary antibody stock solution.
Pipette 198 µl of 0.1% BSA solution into a tube.
Add 2 µl of the secondary antibody to produce a 1:100 (secondary antibody: 0.1% BSA) solution.
Mix well and pipette 50 µl of this stock solution onto the scaffold.
Cover the scaffold with paraffin film.
Wrap the dish with aluminum foil and store at room temperature for 2 hr.
Wash 3x with 2 ml PBS.
Prepare a rhodamine or fluorescein labeled phalloidin stock solution in 0.1% BSA solution.
Pipette 25 µl of each solution into a tube and mix well.
Pipette 200 µl of 0.2% DAPI solution onto the scaffold.
Keep at room temperature for 2-3 min.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil.
Wash 2x with 2 ml PBS.
Place a drop of mounting media on the substrate using a dropper.
Carefully place the scaffold on a glass slide.
Image the scaffold using CLSM.
Extract RNA from cells as follows: Place the scaffold in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pipette 1 ml of an RNA extraction solution into the tube and sonicate for 5 min at room temperature (RT).
Pipette 200 µl of chloroform into each tube, shake vigorously for 15-20 seconds.
Keep tubes at RT for ~3 minutes until phases separate.
Centrifuge the sample at 13,000 x g, 4°C for 15 min and carefully remove supernatant to avoid mixing phases.
Pipette 500-600 µl of the upper aqueous phase into a second microcentrifuge tube.
Add an equivalent volume (500-600 μl) of isopropanol, invert the tube 3-5 times and leave standing at RT for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 13,000 x g, 4°C for 15 min.
If no pellet is visible, centrifuge again for 5 minutes.
Invert tubes with cap open to discard supernatant and pipette in 1 ml of 70% ethanol diluted in DEPC water into the tube.
Slightly vortex the tube to detach the pellet from the wall of the tube.
Let the tube air dry.
Add 50 µl of DPEC water to resuspend the pellet.
Pipette until the pellet dissolves completely.
Incubate for 10 min at 55 °C to denature double-stranded RNA into single-stranded RNA.
Centrifuge the tubes briefly (7,500 x g, 4 min, 4 °C).
Keep the tubes in ice until performing reverse transcriptase and real-time PCR.
